name: Fictitious revenue (shell sales)
how_it_works: Sales are recorded with no underlying economic event — fictitious invoices, sometimes routed through shell entities that return confirmations. Receivables age and are eventually written off or 'settled' with credit notes.
red_flags: ["Revenue growth far ahead of cash collection", "Receivables days climbing while revenue soars", "Unusual customers with no verifiable business presence", "Heavy credit-note activity after year-end", "Sales concentrated with a few new customers"]
pressure: Meeting growth targets, bonus thresholds, listing requirements.
opportunity: Weak customer onboarding; confirmations not controlled by the auditor.
rationalization: 'We'll make it up with real sales next quarter.'
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Channel stuffing
how_it_works: Excess product is pushed to distributors at period-end with generous return rights or side agreements, inflating current-period revenue at the expense of future periods.
red_flags: ["Period-end sales spike to distributors", "Rising returns/credit notes in the next period", "Distributor inventory levels inconsistent with end demand", "Unusual discounting at period-end"]
pressure: Quarterly targets; sales-team incentives paid on shipments.
opportunity: Distributors willing to accept stock; weak returns monitoring.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Bill-and-hold abuse
how_it_works: Revenue is recognised on goods billed but not shipped, where the bill-and-hold criteria (transfer of control, genuine business reason, separately identified goods) are not actually met.
red_flags: ["Bill-and-hold sales concentrated at period-end", "No written customer request for delayed delivery", "Goods not segregated or identifiable", "Customer lacks a substantive reason for the arrangement"]
rationalization: 'The customer has committed — shipment is a formality.'
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Round-tripping
how_it_works: Two parties buy from and sell to each other (directly or via intermediaries), inflating both revenue and expenses with no economic substance — sometimes to fabricate growth, sometimes to launder funds.
red_flags: ["Matched purchases and sales with the same counterparty", "Transactions with no commercial logic", "Circular fund flows", "Counterparties with shared directors/addresses"]
pressure: Revenue growth narrative; hiding related-party dependence.
opportunity: Complex supply chains; weak related-party identification.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Cookie-jar reserves / big bath
how_it_works: In good years, excessive provisions are created (the 'cookie jar'); in bad years they are released to smooth earnings. A 'big bath' takes all possible write-offs in one bad year so future years look better.
red_flags: ["Provisions consistently released in weak quarters", "One-off charges far exceeding peers", "Estimate changes always in the favourable direction", "New management taking a 'clean-up' charge"]
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Cash skimming
how_it_works: Cash is stolen before it is recorded — unrecorded sales, pocketed takings, under-rung registers. Because nothing is recorded, the fraud is invisible to ledger-based testing.
red_flags: ["Cash businesses with weak segregation", "Lifestyle inconsistent with income", "Missing sequentially-numbered documents", "Revenue per unit below peers/benchmarks"]
pressure: Personal financial difficulty; low pay with cash access.
opportunity: One person handles cash, records and reconciles.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Lapping (receivables)
how_it_works: Customer A's payment is stolen; customer B's later payment is credited to A; C's payment covers B — a rolling cover-up that collapses when the chain breaks.
red_flags: ["Persistent small differences on customer accounts", "Customer complaints about misapplied payments", "One person controls receipts and ledger postings", "Delayed banking of receipts"]
opportunity: No segregation between cash handling and receivables ledger.
rationalization: 'I'll pay it back before anyone notices.'
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Ghost employees
how_it_works: Fictitious (or departed) employees remain on the payroll; their wages are diverted to the fraudster. Enabled by weak starter/leaver controls and master-file access.
red_flags: ["Employees with no HR file or with duplicate bank details", "Payroll headcount exceeds HR records", "Unclaimed wages accumulating", "Master-file amendments by payroll staff without approval"]
pressure: Financial need; opportunity seen as low-risk.
opportunity: Payroll clerk can add employees and process payments.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Procurement fraud and kickbacks
how_it_works: Buyer colludes with a supplier: inflated prices, fictitious suppliers, or split orders to avoid approval thresholds — with kickbacks to the buyer. Approved-supplier lists and competitive tendering are bypassed.
red_flags: ["Supplier with no physical presence or shared address with staff", "Prices above market without justification", "Orders split just below approval limits", "Single-source awards without documented rationale", "Supplier bank details changed without verification"]
opportunity: Buyer controls supplier setup and ordering.
rationalization: 'Everyone does it; the company still gets the goods.'
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library

name: Management override via journals
how_it_works: Senior management posts or directs manual journals that bypass controls — backdated, round-sum, or to seldom-used accounts — to achieve a reporting outcome. ISA 240 treats this as a presumed fraud risk on every audit.
red_flags: ["Journals posted outside business hours or in closed periods", "Round-sum or just-below-threshold entries", "Journals by senior management without supporting documents", "Entries to unusual account combinations"]
pressure: Earnings targets; debt covenants; personal wealth tied to results.
opportunity: Unrestricted journal access; weak review of manual entries.
source_ref: CA Audit Intelligence Database — fraud pattern library
